video_caption: The video begins with a vibrant green screen displaying the white text "Price Elasticity of Demand." This transitions to a white background featuring a large, blue, hand-drawn question mark. Next, a pattern of numerous hand-drawn dollar signs in green and dark green fills the screen, suggesting money or revenue. Following this, a simple cartoon drawing of a brown, monkey-like figure wearing a white beanie and a white face mask appears, surrounded by purple question marks. Two price tags, one green labeled "MARK-UP!" and one red labeled "DISCOUNT!", are attached to the monkey by strings, indicating a pricing dilemma. The scene then shifts to a cartoon storefront labeled "STORYBOOKS," with "OPEN" on the door and "1998" below it, displaying books in the windows. Subsequently, two cartoon women's heads are shown facing each other. The woman on the left has curly brown hair, green glasses, and orange earrings, appearing thoughtful or concerned, while the woman on the right has straight blonde hair and a smiling expression. Above the blonde woman's head, a thought bubble contains a price tag with a question mark, surrounded by plus and minus signs, visually representing a decision about pricing strategies. Finally, the scene zooms in on the thoughtful woman with the curly brown hair and green glasses, who now has the thought bubble above her head, continuing to ponder the pricing question.

A cartoon drawing of a person's head with brown curly hair, green glasses, and a neutral expression is centered on a white background. A thought bubble above their head contains question marks, plus signs, and minus signs, conveying a sense of confusion or deliberation.

The video segment opens with a black and white drawing of a newspaper headline that reads, "TRAVEL BARGAINS-AIRLINES SLASH FARES!" (This headline suggests that airlines have reduced their prices for travel). The scene then transitions to a green background where the newspaper drawing appears as a green outline. Over this, white text states, "LAW OF DEMAND: More of a good will be bought the lower its price, less will be bought the higher its price, ceteris paribus." (This explains the economic principle that as price decreases, demand increases, and vice versa, assuming all other factors remain constant). The background shifts to white, and a simple stick figure drawing of a head with wide eyes and a neutral expression appears, accompanied by a thought bubble containing a red question mark. This is followed by a full-body drawing of a brown sock monkey wearing a white and red striped hat, with a price tag attached that initially shows "$5" and then changes to "$10", indicating a price increase. A stick figure with a sad expression and raised hands then appears next to the monkey, looking displeased. This sad stick figure is next seen holding a smaller, faded version of the sock monkey, symbolizing a reduced purchase or loss of customers. Finally, a different stick figure with a happy, smiling face and outstretched arms holding two fans of green dollar bills appears, representing increased revenue, suggesting that a price increase, if not too significant to deter buyers, can lead to higher earnings.

The video segment begins on a bright green background displaying white text that reads: "(Price) Elasticity of Demand measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the product price." (This text defines the concept of price elasticity of demand). At 00:06, the background quickly transitions to white, and a clear mathematical formula `e_d = (%ΔQ_d) / (%ΔP)` appears on the screen (This formula represents the price elasticity of demand, where `e_d` is elasticity of demand, `%ΔQ_d` is the percentage change in quantity demanded, and `%ΔP` is the percentage change in price). As an unseen speaker explains that demand exhibits an inverse relationship, at 00:20, this formula is briefly overlaid and then replaced by the inequality `e_d < 0` (This signifies that the price elasticity of demand is typically a negative value, reflecting the inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded). This inequality remains on screen until 00:25, when the original formula `e_d = (%ΔQ_d) / (%ΔP)` reappears and stays on the white background until the end of the segment.

The video segment features two simple cartoon heads, one on the left with a broadly smiling, happy expression and the other on the right looking confused, with a question mark floating above its head. A thought bubble hovers above both, containing a stylized green dollar bill with a large "1" (one) in the center, representing a $1 change. The narrator discusses whether this $1 change is significant, leading to the conclusion that "it depends," suggesting that context is crucial for evaluating the magnitude of the change.

The video segment opens with a newspaper article from the "Christian Science Monitor" dated September 18, 1997, titled "Clinton Targets Teen Smoking," authored by the Associated Press. The article discusses President Clinton's efforts to reduce teen smoking by proposing measures such as raising cigarette prices by $1.50 per pack and implementing harsher penalties for tobacco firms marketing to teens. From 0:09, the last paragraph of the article is highlighted in yellow, stating: "Papers accompanying the announcement cited estimates that a 10 percent increase in cigarette prices will lead to a 7 percent drop in youth smoking. Clinton also said the Food and Drug Administration should have full regulatory power over tobacco." (This highlighted text provides key data for an economic calculation.) A female voice narrates, explaining that this information is sufficient to determine the elasticity of demand for youth smoking. At 0:17, the newspaper article fades out, transitioning to a plain white screen displaying a mathematical formula in black text: "e_d = (%ΔQ_d) / (%ΔP)" (This is the formula for price elasticity of demand, where e_d represents elasticity of demand, %ΔQ_d is the percentage change in quantity demanded, and %ΔP is the percentage change in price). The female voice continues, saying, "Remember, elasticity of demand is the..." before the segment concludes.

The video segment displays a series of mathematical equations on a plain white background, illustrating the calculation of price elasticity of demand. Initially, the black text " % Δ P = +10% " (Percentage change in price = +10%) appears, signifying a 10% increase in price. This text then fades out as new black text " % Δ Q_d = -7% " (Percentage change in quantity demanded = -7%) appears, indicating a 7% decrease in the quantity demanded. Next, the formula for elasticity of demand, " e_d = % Δ Q_d / % Δ P " (Elasticity of demand = Percentage change in quantity demanded / Percentage change in price), is presented. The numerical values are then substituted into the formula, showing " e_d = -7% / +10% " (Elasticity of demand = -7% / +10%). Finally, the calculated result " e_d = -.7 " (Elasticity of demand = -0.7) is displayed prominently on the screen.

The video segment opens on a white screen displaying the formula `e_d = -.7`. The letters `e_d` then grow in size and turn orange with a black outline, as a stick figure with a distressed expression and head-scratching gesture appears to the right. This stick figure shrinks and adopts a relaxed, leaning pose as the `e_d = -.7` text reappears and the negative sign is highlighted by a red circle and arrow. A graph titled "PRICE(P)" vs. "QUANTITY DEMANDED (Qd)" with a downward-sloping demand curve then appears in the background, showing points (P1, Q1) and (P2, Q2). The negative sign and arrow fade, and the formula `|e_d| = .7` appears, soon overlaid by a large blue question mark that then disappears, replaced by the number `1`. The formula `|e_d| = .7` reappears, then transitions to `|e_d| < 1`. This inequality leads to the full formula for elasticity of demand `e_d = (%ΔQ_d) / (%ΔP)` appearing, which then transforms into `|(%ΔQ_d) / (%ΔP)| < 1`. This further simplifies to `|%ΔQ_d| < |%ΔP|`, where the percentage and delta symbols enlarge and turn purple, and a yawning stick figure appears next to them. The screen then turns orange, and the text "TIME TO THINK" appears in white. This text fades slightly, revealing two childlike stick figures (a boy in a red cap and a girl with red bows) on the left. The "TIME TO THINK" text disappears, and two adult stick figures (a man holding a brown briefcase and a woman) appear on the right. The "TIME TO THINK" text briefly reappears faintly over the children, then fully covers the screen again on an orange background. The video ends with "TIME TO THINK" (in white on an orange background) fading to a black screen accompanied by a beep.

The video segment opens with two stick figures, a boy wearing a red cap and a girl in an orange dress, enclosed within a red circle on the left, representing "youth." To their right stand two adult stick figures, a man holding a brown briefcase and a woman in a blue dress. As the video progresses, the adult male fades, and thought bubbles appear above the remaining stick figures. The adult woman's thought bubble contains three stacks of money, while the girl's thought bubble contains one stack of money, illustrating that adults tend to have more disposable income. Next, the money thought bubbles fade. The adult woman is then shown on the right with a cigarette in her mouth. Her thought bubble depicts the girl, also with a cigarette, surrounded by various years (1994, 1995, 1996, 1997, 1998, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009), suggesting the adult has been smoking for a longer period. Finally, all the stick figures and thought bubbles fade out, and a mathematical inequality appears on screen: "|e_d^adult| < |e_d^youth|". This text means "the absolute value of the elasticity of demand for adults is less than the absolute value of the elasticity of demand for youth", signifying that adults' demand for the product (implied to be cigarettes) is less elastic than that of youth.

The video opens with a hand-drawn, blue question mark against a plain white background, symbolizing an unanswered query. This transitions to the same question mark fading slightly as the black mathematical text `|e_d| < 1` appears over it, representing "the absolute value of the elasticity of demand is less than one." The question mark then disappears, leaving only the mathematical expression on the white screen. Finally, this text fades out, replaced by a simple cartoon drawing: a circular face with wide eyes and a somewhat confused expression is centered on the screen, surrounded by small floating question marks. Above the face, two cloud-like thought bubbles appear; the left one contains an upward arrow, while the right one contains a downward arrow, posing the dilemma of whether to raise or lower a price.

The video opens with a static shot of a bright blue sky filled with white clouds, where the sun shines brightly, creating lens flares. A wooden utility pole with electrical wires and two grey cylindrical transformers stands in the foreground, with green foliage at the bottom. This scene then transitions to an overlay featuring a startled stick figure looking at a newspaper. The newspaper's headline reads "ELECTRIC CO. RATE INCREASE OF 11% APPROVED!". The background fades to white, showing only the stick figure and the newspaper. This then gives way to a glowing hand-drawn incandescent light bulb, which quickly transforms into a glowing spiral-shaped compact fluorescent lamp (CFL) bulb. Next, a hand-drawn graph appears on a white background, with the Y-axis labeled "kW.hr" and the X-axis labeled "time" with months from January to December. A red line on the graph shows a relatively flat consumption until May, where an arrow points to the line with red text stating "Rate increase imposed - SLIGHT decrease in consumption," indicating a minimal drop in consumption. A stick figure, acting as a presenter, appears on the left, holding a pointer stick towards a whiteboard with a "SALES" graph that initially shows a flat red line. Subsequently, a green line with an upward arrow is drawn over the "SALES" graph, representing an increase. The word "REVENUES" also appears above "SALES" with an upward arrow, further emphasizing growth. Finally, large pink text "TR = P x Q" (Total Revenue equals Price times Quantity) is prominently displayed over the presenter and the graph.

The video segment begins with a white screen displaying the mathematical expression "|e_d| > 1" (The absolute value of e sub d is greater than 1). This then transforms into "|%ΔQ_d / %ΔP| > 1" (The absolute value of the percentage change in quantity demanded over the percentage change in price is greater than 1). The previous expression is briefly visible behind it. The equation simplifies to "|%ΔQ_d| > |%ΔP|" (The absolute value of the percentage change in quantity demanded is greater than the absolute value of the percentage change in price) on a white background, with a faint outline of the previous fraction still visible. This transitions to a cartoon stick figure on the right, wide-eyed and hands on its head, reacting to a newspaper on the left with the headline "PRICE RISES BY 2 PERCENT". Small question marks are scattered around the figure. The screen then changes to an orange background with the bold white text "TIME TO THINK" appearing centrally, with the previous cartoon elements faintly visible. The background returns to white, showing the same cartoon stick figure, now with a puzzled expression, surrounded by question marks and two thought bubbles containing an upward and a downward arrow respectively. This cartoon fades into a real photo of an American Airlines airplane taking off against a dramatic sky with orange and pink clouds. The airplane image fades to reveal a cartoon newspaper with the headline "AIRFARE DISCOUNT 5%". Finally, a stick figure is shown presenting a graph titled "SALES" with an upward-sloping red line. This graph then updates to "REVENUES" with a new upward-sloping green line, indicating an increase.

The video segment opens with a stick figure cartoon character, with closed eyes and an open mouth as if speaking, pointing a stick towards a blackboard-like rectangle on the right. Inside the rectangle, a graph shows "REVENUES" (English) on the vertical axis with a green upward-sloping line, representing increasing revenues. Faintly visible behind this, the text "|ed| = 1" (English) and "ed" (English) are present, introducing the concept of unit elastic demand. This transitions to a full-screen display of the equation "|ed| = 1" (English) in bold black text on a white background, mathematically defining unit elastic demand. The scene then shows another equation, "|%ΔQd| = |%ΔP|" (English), which means "the absolute value of the percentage change in quantity demanded equals the absolute value of the percentage change in price," illustrating that unit elasticity implies equal percentage changes in quantity demanded and price, with the previous equation fading behind it. The view returns to the stick figure pointing at the blackboard, which now displays two separate graphs: one labeled "PRICE" (English) with a blue upward-sloping line marked "+10%" (English), indicating a 10% increase in price, and another labeled "SALES" (English) with a red downward-sloping line marked "-10%" (English), showing a 10% decrease in sales or quantity demanded. The equation "|%ΔQd| = |%ΔP|" (English) again appears faintly behind these graphs. Finally, the "PRICE" and "SALES" graphs fade out, replaced by the "REVENUES" graph from the beginning, but this time the green line is horizontal, indicating no change in total revenue when elasticity of demand is one.
